title: 第11章 深渊的回声第12章 锈蚀的剑刃
slug: 黯潮纪元异世界的崛起
content_zh:
伊格纳修斯推开门时，陈默闻到一股茶香。
不是银月城常见的薄荷茶。是带着烟熏味的红茶，像他在三星堆考古站熬夜泡的那种。这个认知让后颈发麻——穿越者不该有这种嗅觉记忆。
“请坐。”
会客厅不大，但挑高惊人。四面墙壁从腰部以上全是壁画，圣光从无数个角度散射开来，像太阳爆炸的瞬间被定格。陈默在沙发上坐下，接过茶杯。瓷壁烫手，他换了个姿势才稳住。
伊格纳修斯在他对面落座，给自己也倒了一杯。动作很慢，像在给陈默时间观察这个房间。
“审判庭的结论已经出来了。”
陈默没有接话。
“第三骑士小队缺一个正式编制骑士。”伊格纳修斯抿了一口茶，“你被编进去了。明天早上报到。”
就这么简单。没有解释，没有条件，没有“你是否愿意”。陈默盯着茶杯里漂浮的茶叶碎片，忽然意识到自己从穿越那一刻起，就没有真正做过选择。
“队长是艾莉安娜·格雷。”
伊格纳修斯说这个名字时语气没有任何变化。但陈默注意到他端茶的手停了一瞬——半秒。足够让一个考古学家的眼睛捕捉到。
“她曾是阿尔德里奇的学生。”
陈默的手指收紧。茶杯里的水面晃动起来。
伊格纳修斯放下茶杯，站起身，走到壁画前。白袍下摆扫过地面，发出轻微的沙沙声。陈默跟着站起来，目光扫过那幅巨大的圣光辐射图——从中心向外扩散的纹路呈螺旋状延伸，像一朵绽放的花。
不。不是花。是螺旋。
和阿尔德里奇留在屋顶上的符文一模一样。但方向相反。那个符文是顺时针向内收拢，这壁画是逆时针向外扩散。
一个在吸。一个在放。
“圣光来自更高的意志。”伊格纳修斯背对着他说，“我们只是通道。不是源头。”
陈默盯着壁画上的螺旋纹路，脑子里有什么东西在拼凑。阿尔德里奇符文中的螺旋结构——顺时针，向内收拢——像是在把什么东西吸进去。而这壁画上的螺旋是逆时针向外扩散——像是在释放什么东西。
两个方向，两种用途。

“阿尔德里奇曾经也是审判庭的人。”伊格纳修斯转过身，目光平静得像一潭死水，“他走得太远了。”
陈默想问“多远才算远”，但他没有开口。他看见伊格纳修斯的眼睛里有一瞬间闪过某种东西——不是悲伤，不是愤怒，是更接近恐惧的情绪。
“明天早上，第三小队驻地。”伊格纳修斯走向门口，“东区旧神殿。”
他推开门，回头看了一眼。这一次他没有重复那句话，只是说：“你会有很多问题。格雷队长会给你答案。”
门关上了。
陈默站在原地，听着脚步声远去。茶杯里的茶已经凉了。他低头看，水面上映着自己的脸——不对，是雷诺的脸，五官陌生，眼神熟悉。
他忽然想起阿尔德里奇的警告。
别相信任何人。
***
东区旧神殿的门口堆着废弃的石料。
陈默站在台阶下，看着这座建筑。它曾经供奉过什么神——从残留的浮雕轮廓来看，那东西有触手，有眼睛，有不该属于这个世界的扭曲形态。后来被凿掉了。留下的凹痕像伤疤，填补着新的圣光浮雕，但新旧之间总有裂缝。
门是开着的。
陈默走进去，闻到一股霉味和圣光燃烧后的焦糊味。大厅里空荡荡的，只有几张桌椅随意摆放，墙角的武器架上插着几把剑，其中一把的剑刃上有缺口。
“新来的？”
声音从左侧传来。陈默转头，看见一个男人靠在门框上，三十出头，褐发乱糟糟地扎在脑后，脸上挂着笑。他穿着骑士制式的锁甲，但没系腰带，敞着衣襟露出里面的旧衬衫。
“托马斯·贝克特，副队长。”他走过来，伸出手，“你是陈默吧？伊格纳修斯的人今早来通知过。”
陈默握住他的手。托马斯的手掌粗糙，指节上有老茧，是常年握剑的手。
“队长在楼上等你。”托马斯朝楼梯方向努了努嘴，“上去吧。她不喜欢等人。”
陈默上楼时听见身后传来托马斯的笑声：“别紧张，她不吃人——最多咬一口。”
楼梯是石砌的，踩上去有回音。二楼走廊两侧有几扇门，其中一扇开着。陈默走过去，看见里面是一个小厅，窗边站着一个人。
content_en:
When Ignatius opened the door, Chen Mo smelled the aroma of tea.
This is not the common mint tea in Silvermoon City. It's black tea with a smoky flavor, like the one he stayed up late brewing at the Sanxingdui Archaeological Station. The realization made the back of the neck tingle - a time traveler shouldn't have this kind of olfactory memory.
"Please take a seat."
The living room is not big, but the ceiling is amazing. The four walls are covered with murals from the waist up. The holy light scatters from countless angles, like the moment when the sun explodes. Chen Mo sat down on the sofa and took the tea cup. The porcelain wall was hot to the touch, so he changed his position to stabilize himself.
Ignatius sat down opposite him and poured himself a glass. The movement was very slow, as if giving Chen Mo time to observe the room.
"The trial court's conclusion has been reached."
Chen Mo didn't answer.
"The third knight squad is short of a formal knight." Ignatius took a sip of tea, "You are included. Report for duty tomorrow morning."
It's that simple. No explanation, no conditions, no "would you rather". Chen Mo stared at the fragments of tea leaves floating in the tea cup, and suddenly realized that he had never really made a choice from the moment he traveled through time.
"The captain is Ariana Grey."
Ignatius said the name without any change in his tone. But Chen Mo noticed that his hand holding the tea stopped for a moment - half a second. Enough for an archaeologist's eye to catch.
"She was a student of Aldridge's."
Chen Mo tightened his fingers. The water in the tea cup sloshed.
Ignatius put down his tea cup, stood up, and walked to the mural. The hem of the white robe swept across the ground, making a slight rustling sound. Chen Mo stood up and scanned the huge holy light radiation diagram - the lines spreading out from the center extended in a spiral, like a blooming flower.
No. Not flowers. It's a spiral.
It's exactly the same rune Aldridge left on the roof. But in the opposite direction. The rune is closing inward clockwise, while the mural is spreading outward counterclockwise.
One is sucking. One is playing.
"The Holy Light comes from a higher will." Ignatius turned his back to him and said, "We are only channels. Not the source."
Chen Mo stared at the spiral patterns on the mural, piecing together something in his mind. The spiral structure in Aldridge's rune—clockwise, inward—seems to be sucking something in. The spiral on this mural spreads outward in a counterclockwise direction - as if it is releasing something.
Two directions, two uses.
"Aldridge was once a member of the Tribunal." Ignatius turned around, his eyes as calm as a pool of stagnant water, "He went too far."
Chen Mo wanted to ask "How far is far?" but he didn't ask. He saw something flash in Ignatius' eyes for a moment - not sadness, not anger, but something closer to fear.
"Tomorrow morning, the third team will be stationed." Ignatius walked towards the door, "Old Temple in the East District."
He opened the door and looked back. This time he didn't repeat the words, just said, "You're going to have a lot of questions. Captain Gray will give you the answers."
The door is closed.
Chen Mo stood there, listening to the footsteps going away. The tea in the cup has gone cold. He looked down and saw his own face reflected in the water - no, it was Renault's face, with unfamiliar features and familiar eyes.
He suddenly remembered Aldridge's warning.
Don't trust anyone.
***
Abandoned stones are piled at the entrance of the old temple in the East District.
Chen Mo stood at the foot of the steps and looked at the building. It once enshrined some god—judging from the remaining relief outlines, that thing had tentacles, eyes, and a twisted form that should not belong to this world. It was later chiseled away. The dents left behind are like scars, filled with new light reliefs, but there are always cracks between the old and the new.
The door is open.
Chen Mo walked in and smelled a musty smell and the burnt smell of the burning holy light. The hall is empty except for a fewTables and chairs were placed randomly, and there were several swords stuck in the weapon racks in the corner, one of which had a notch on the blade.
"New here?"
The voice came from the left. Chen Mo turned his head and saw a man leaning against the door frame. He was in his early thirties, with messy brown hair tied back, and a smile on his face. He wore knightly mail, but without a belt, and his coat was open to reveal an old shirt underneath.
"Thomas Beckett, deputy captain." He walked over and stretched out his hand, "Are you Chen Mo? Ignatius' people came to inform you this morning."
Chen Mo held his hand. Thomas's palms were rough, with calluses on the knuckles, from hands that had been holding swords all year round.
"The captain is waiting for you upstairs." Thomas pursed his lips toward the stairs, "Go up. She doesn't like waiting for people."
When Chen Mo went upstairs, he heard Thomas' laughter behind him: "Don't be nervous, she doesn't eat people - she can only take one bite."
The stairs are made of stone, and there is an echo when you step on them. There are several doors on both sides of the corridor on the second floor, one of which is open. Chen Mo walked over and saw a small hall inside, with a person standing by the window.
